description:
## Outcome

        Agent, scenario, suite, and command data can select a trusted execution profile by ID only. The CLI applies one documented precedence rule and gives Jidoka a `PolicyRequest`.

        ## Why now

        Users need profile selection, but raw backend configuration must never enter data files. The selection format must be fixed before environments run.

        ## Current state

        Agent entries and `--runtime-profile` can name a CLI profile, but `Plan` resolves the name to arbitrary import and run options. Jidoka `Import.AgentDocument` and `Agent.Spec` have no typed execution-profile selector. Scenario data has no selector. Unknown CLI profiles already return a configuration error.

        ## Ownership and boundary

        Both repositories change. Jidoka owns an inert agent selector and its import/export projection. The CLI owns scenario, suite, and command parsing, precedence, trusted host resolver injection, and exit 64. Neither data format can name a module, command, image, mount, network policy, or adapter.

        ## Detailed implementation

        1. In Jidoka, add one versioned agent field such as `execution_profile: STRING` or `execution_environment: {profile: STRING}`. Keep it inert through import, spec, projection, and export.
2. In the CLI version-1 loaders, add the same ID-only selector to scenario and suite run data. Keep the current command option as the explicit override.
3. Apply precedence: command override, then scenario, then agent, then suite default, then none. Document this exact order. If a safer conflict rule is selected, use it consistently and update this story before coding.
4. Resolve the selected ID through the injected trusted Jidoka resolver. Pass only the resulting policy request and resolved registration to the engine.
5. Remove arbitrary data-driven import/run option injection from the public profile path. Keep test-only injected capabilities separate.
6. Return stable configuration errors before Plan opens an output directory or calls an engine.

        ## Acceptance criteria

        - [ ] Every input surface accepts a valid profile ID and rejects other shapes.
- [ ] The documented precedence is deterministic.
- [ ] Agent import/export round-trips the inert selector.
- [ ] Unknown, disabled, malformed, or insufficient profiles fail before execution with status 64.
- [ ] Raw backend keys in agent, scenario, or suite documents fail validation.
- [ ] Test injection of fake LLM and adapter capabilities remains possible through host opts, not data.

        ## Test plan

        - Success: one case for each selector source and every precedence pair.
- Invalid input: non-string ID, unknown field, raw command/image/mount/network/backend map, and conflicting data.
- Runtime failure: resolver raises or registration becomes unavailable before engine start.
- Boundary and security: assert no input value becomes a module, executable, environment variable, or raw adapter option.
- Deterministic capability: inject resolver, profiles, adapters, and IDs.
- JSONL and exit status: configuration failures write no stdout JSONL, use stderr diagnostics, and exit 64.

        ## Documentation

        Update Jidoka import/export docs and CLI README examples. Add a trusted host configuration example that is clearly separate from agent and scenario data.

        ## Non-goals

        Do not start an environment. Do not add raw policy fields. Do not change scenario schema beyond the selector. Do not add project trust yet.

        ## Dependencies

        Blocking issues:

        - `jido_cli-tqg.3.3` — Resolve trusted security profiles and fail closed
- `jido_cli-tqg.2.2` — Run automation cells through the public Jidoka sequence

        Features unlocked by this story:

        - Constrained automation cell execution
- Safe default coding profiles
- Trusted replay profiles

        ## Commit plan

        Create exactly two focused commits because the repositories have separate histories. First create one `jidoka` commit such as `feat(jidoka): add trusted execution-profile selection (jido_cli-tqg.3.6)`. Then create one `jido_cli` commit such as `feat(cli): integrate add trusted execution-profile selection (jido_cli-tqg.3.6)`. Do not include another backlog feature in either commit.

        ## Verification commands

        ```sh
        cd /Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_cli/jidoka
mix test test/jidoka/import_test.exs test/jidoka/golden/import_to_spec_test.exs
mix quality
mix test
mix docs
cd /Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_cli/jido_cli
mix test test/jido_cli/cli/automation/loader_test.exs test/jido_cli/cli/automation/plan_test.exs test/jido_cli/cli_test.exs
mix quality
mix test --cover
mix docs
        ```
title: Add data-only execution-profile selection and precedence
